host.power: laptop on battery, Windows 'Balanced' plan (CPU throttled); WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04

role: Llama writes the explanation; risk and steps come from the grounded rules

cases.summary: The EV charger is a secure device that runs authentic firmware and has no known vulnerabilities, and its network behavior matches its baseline. This matters because it indicates that the charger is a trusted and reliable device, and its security is not a concern.
steps: ChargeGuard keeps monitoring the session for changes in behaviour.

cases.summary: The EV charger's firmware was modified without the vendor's signature, and the software was released without a known version number. This compromised the charger's integrity and security.
steps: Do not authorise charging on this unit.
Reflash the latest vendor-signed firmware through the vendor's update tool.
Keep the evidence report: it records the measured firmware and why it failed.

cases.summary: The EV charger contains two known vulnerabilities in OpenSSL and zlib, which are serious security issues.
steps: Charging can continue, but schedule a firmware upgrade.
Ask the vendor for a release that includes: 1.1.1l, 1.2.12.
Re-verify the charger after the upgrade; it should then show green.

cases.summary: The EV charger started communicating in ways it shouldn't, using a port scan to connect to a specific IP address. This was done to protect the network, and the charger was isolated from the network as a precaution.
steps: Leave the charger isolated; the session was stopped safely.
Collect the evidence report and network capture for your security team.
Reflash vendor firmware and rotate any credentials stored on the unit before reconnecting.

cases.summary: This message is very likely a scam because its wording matches common scam messages (your, a web link, now) and it links to chargepoint-billing.top, which looks like a fake site.
steps: Do not reply, call back or open the link.
Check your account only in the official app or website you normally use.
Delete the message, or report it as spam to your mobile operator.

cases.summary: This link is NOT safe: it is very likely a phishing (fake) page because it is very likely a fake page (credential or payment keyword in path; brand name used outside the brand's own domain). Do not open this link.
steps: Do not enter card details, passwords or one-time codes on this site.
Pay only through the charging operator's official app or the charger's own payment terminal.
If it came from a QR sticker on a charger, report the charger to the site operator.

cases.summary: This link looks safe because it is on ChargeGuard's list of known official sites.
steps: Still check the address bar before entering payment details.

note: Development-host figures, not Raspberry Pi 5. On mains power the same host measured about 25 tok/s decode, 0.6-0.8 s to first token and 260-290 tok/s prefill. Explanations that fail the grounding check are replaced by the grounded template; none failed in this run.
